output.answer_markdown: Visa describes its pension plan market risk as follows: a material adverse decline in pension plan asset values and/or in the discount rate for benefit obligations would decrease the funded status of the pension plans, increase pension cost and increase required funding [1]. For the U.S. plans, a hypothetical 10% decrease in asset values and a 1% decrease in the discount rate as of September 30, 2022 would decrease aggregate funded status by approximately $150 million and increase pension cost by approximately $32 million [2]. For the non-U.S. plans, the same hypothetical scenario as of September 30, 2022 would decrease aggregate funded status by approximately $82 million and increase pension cost by approximately $11 million [3].

provenance.quote: A material adverse decline in the value of pension plan assets and/or in the discount rate for benefit obligations would result in a decrease in the funded status of the pension plans, an increase in pension cost and an increase in required funding.
